newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF hikes dividend as net profit up 13 percent.
newsitem.headline: BASF hikes dividend as net profit up 13 percent.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG on Tuesday reported stronger-than-expected 1996 earnings and said it planned to raise its dividend for the year to 1.70 marks per share from 1.40 marks.
Group net profit rose 12.9 percent to 2.79 billion marks ($1.7 billion) from 2.47 billion marks, BASF said in a statement.
Pre-tax profit climbed 6.9 percent to 4.41 billion marks from 4.13 billion, above analysts' forecasts for a five percent rise on average.
The dividend payout also beat forecasts for a figure of 1.60 marks.

The news initially boosted BASF's share price which briefly rose 0.35 percent to 63.78 marks but the gains quickly evaporated and the share were quoted at 62.40 marks at 1200 GMT, down 0.95 marks on the day.
BASF said its group sales rose 5.5 percent to 48.78 billion marks from 46.23 billion, above forecasts for a 3.5 percent rise.

The company also said its dividend payout rose 23.1 percent to 1.05 billion marks from 854 million and that it transferred 650 million marks of its 1996 earnings to reserves, up 30 percent from the year earlier.
BASF will detail its results at a news conference on April 2. ($ = 1.690 German Marks)
